characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL; Co-Kα source; operating voltage 40 kV; operating current 40 mA
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 0 h pre-mixed powder shows the diffraction peaks of the individual elements Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si and C, which diminish with increasing milling time; many elemental diffraction peaks co-exist at almost the same d-spacing (Supplementary Fig. S1).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Pre-mixed elemental powder at 0 h; scan rate 5°/min; 2θ range approximately 20°-100°
characterization_methods.purpose: To study the alloying behavior as a function of milling time and to characterize the starting pre-mixed powder (0 h)

analytical_models.model_name: Melting point by machine learning (ML) approach
analytical_models.model_note: Reported as more precise and accurate than the rule of mixture.

analytical_models.equation_role: Melting point estimated by the rule of mixture

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Binary liquidus temperatures of the constituent binary alloys (Table 1)
computational_details.simulation_method: Machine learning (ML) approach formula and rule of mixture for melting point prediction

analytical_models.equation_role: Criteria for regular solid solution formation in HEAs
analytical_models.model_name: Thermodynamic parameters for solid-solution formation (ΔH_mix, ΔS_conf, δ, Ω, VEC)
analytical_models.model_note: Reference criteria: -22 ≤ ΔH_mix ≤ 7; 11 ≤ ΔS_conf ≤ 19.5; δ ≤ 6.6; Ω ≥ 1.1; VEC < 6.87 BCC, 6.87 < VEC < 8.0 BCC + FCC, VEC ≥ 8.0 FCC. The alloy satisfies ΔH_mix, ΔS_conf and Ω criteria, VEC = 6.9 lies in the BCC + FCC band, but δ = 7.6 % exceeds the δ ≤ 6.6 % limit.

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Binary mixing enthalpies (semi-empirical Miedema approach, Table 1)
computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic parameter calculation based on the Boltzmann hypothesis, Miedema model and Zhang's approach
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated parameters lie within the random solid solution formation criteria; VEC = 6.9 is within the dual-phase (BCC + FCC) range and the alloy forms BCC/B2 structures in the milled and SPSed samples.

processing_steps.method: pre-mixing/blending of elemental powders (before milling, 0 h)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Starting elemental powders of Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si and C (99.2% pure) were taken in the appropriate proportion of Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (at.%) (Fe-46.00%, Mn-21.50%, Ni-18.13%, Al-8.34%, Si-5.78%, C-0.25%; wt.%). This is the initial powder blend at 0 h, i.e., before any mechanical milling.

structures.overall_structure: Physical mixture (blend) of the individual constituent elemental powders before any milling (0 h). The XRD pattern of the pre-mixed powder at 0 h reveals the diffraction peaks related to the individual elements Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si and C; many diffraction peaks of the alloying elements co-exist at almost the same d-spacing.

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition of the pre-mixed powder (0 h): Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (at.%) corresponding to Fe-46.00%, Mn-21.50%, Ni-18.13%, Al-8.34%, Si-5.78%, C-0.25% (wt.%). [b0020]
The starting elemental Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si and C powders were 99.2% pure. [b0020]

The XRD pattern of the pre-milled (pre-mixed) powder and standard peaks of the elements Fe, Mn, Ni, Al and Si are shown in Supplementary Fig. S1 (a & b); many diffraction peaks of the alloying elements co-exist at almost the same d-spacing. [b0039]

In the pre-mixed powder at 0 h, the diffraction peak intensity of all the elements is highest and these elemental peaks decrease/vanished with milling time; low-intensity peaks of all elements vanished after 5 h of milling and the intensity of Al diminished after 15 h, indicating the highest alloying rate for Al. [b0034, b0038]

Particle size and morphology of the elemental powder blend (0 h) are not explicitly quantified in the text; the first SEM micrograph reported (Fig. 2(a)) corresponds to 10 h milled powder, not to the 0 h pre-mixed state.
